headline: Geopolitical Fog Splits the Tape: Dow Records While Tech and Energy Retreat
body_html:
Wednesday's session ended with a fractured market, as dueling forces pulled equities in opposite directions. Optimism around a potential diplomatic framework governing Hormuz Strait transit rights lifted the Dow to a record close, yet the technology-heavy Nasdaq finished lower, dragged by chipmakers and select large-cap names. Advancing issues in our 549-name universe numbered 242 against 305 decliners — a negative breadth reading that underscored how narrowly the day's gains were distributed.

The clearest rotational story was the flight toward hard assets and rate-sensitive sectors. Materials surged 2.09% to lead all groups, with advanced-materials specialist Materion vaulting nearly 31% after what appeared to be a powerful earnings catalyst. Homebuilders added 1.54%, suggesting some relief trade on the rate-sensitive front. At the other end of the ledger, Semiconductors shed 2.93% and Energy fell 2.63% — a counterintuitive drop for the latter given that U.S. refining margins are reportedly benefiting from Middle East supply disruptions, though traders may have opted to pocket recent war-premium gains.

The session's standout on the downside was SolarEdge, which plummeted more than 30%, matching Materion's gain in magnitude but in the opposite direction. With gold prices jumping and the tape this divided, Wednesday's close reads less like conviction and more like a market still searching for its footing amid an unresolved geopolitical backdrop.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Framework Takes Shape, Lifting Sentiment
briefs.body: Iran and Oman reached an understanding on navigational coordinates through the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's foreign ministry. Reports also indicated a proposed broader deal would hand Tehran authority over inbound vessel traffic — a development that buoyed risk appetite early in the session and helped push the Dow to a fresh record.

briefs.headline: Materion Rockets 31% in Session's Most Dramatic Single-Stock Move
briefs.body: Advanced-materials producer Materion closed up 30.81%, the largest gain in our universe on Wednesday. The surge lifted the broader Materials sector to the top of the leaderboard at plus 2.09%, making it the decisive pocket of strength in an otherwise mixed tape.

briefs.headline: SolarEdge Implodes, Extending Solar Sector's Rough Stretch
briefs.body: SolarEdge dropped 30.48%, the steepest single-session decline across our coverage on Wednesday. The collapse weighed on the clean-energy corner of the technology universe and highlighted the divergence between traditional commodity names, which found buyers, and alternative-energy plays, which did not.

briefs.headline: Shopify Surges Nearly 17% as E-Commerce Momentum Holds
briefs.body: Shopify shares jumped 16.98%, placing the e-commerce platform among the session's top five gainers. The move suggested investors see durable demand in online retail infrastructure even as broader technology names faced selling pressure from semiconductor weakness and concerns over AI talent attrition at select internet giants.

briefs.headline: Healthcare Devices Under Pressure After Dual Earnings Blows
briefs.body: LeMaitre Vascular and Insulet Corporation each reported results that disappointed, sending their shares down 25.32% and 20.12%, respectively. The paired declines confined the broader Healthcare sector to a modest loss of 0.07% for the day, masking what was a punishing afternoon for the medical-devices subsegment.

briefs.headline: Houthi Tanker Attacks Add New Layer to Red Sea Risk Premium
briefs.body: Yemen's Houthi movement claimed responsibility for strikes on Saudi oil tankers operating in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, adding fresh friction to already-disrupted regional shipping lanes. Gulf oil exports remained roughly 40% below pre-war levels in July, data showed, though energy equities fell as traders appeared to rotate out of recent winners rather than chase the headline.
